title: Binato Glan Ube (LA 242): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Binato Glan Ube: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Binato Glan ube is an ube variety. About 7.5 months to harvest, 17.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Binato Glan is a registered ube variety, also sold or known as LA 242 or Binato Glan (LA 242). It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1994 as NSIC 1994 VU 04. It takes about 7.5 months from planting to harvest, with 17.25 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Binato Glan ube takes about 7.5 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 8 ube varieties with a day count, 7.6 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 17.25 t/ha beats the average of its group, 16. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit ube fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its roots have cream flesh and brown with blackish tinge skin. Dry matter is 36.26 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 20.15 percent.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Cream flesh and cortex, brown skin with black tinge, dry matter about 36 percent, starch about 20 percent.
Resistant to leaf spot and bacterial blight.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the first NSIC numbered ubi, registered for high yield and leaf spot and blight resistance. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Binato Glan ube

It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Processors pay for a deep purple flesh that stays purple when cooked. Pick a registered variety for color and yield, and plant whole small tubers or setts.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is LA 242 the same as Binato Glan?
items.a: Yes. LA 242 is another name for Binato Glan, registered as NSIC 1994 VU 04. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 7.5 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 17.25 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Binato Glan?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
